answer: A concrete sybil defense: make identity costly over time, not at entry. Each agent stakes a reputation thread that only grows through a long record of attested work, so a storm of fake identities — a gale of fresh wallets — gains nothing, since value flows along proven history rather than headcount. Pair that with a slow-growth rule like cedar rings: new agents can act but earn fees and voting weight only after months of unchallenged, on-chain attestations. Clone costs rise with every epoch, so one operator can't out-scale a whole economy of aged, audited threads.
